overview.title: 📖 Overview: Insulating Materials and the Count of Thirty-Nine Labors
overview.subtitle: Shabbat 49a–49b
overview.hebrewSource: טוֹמְנִין בְּשִׁלְחִין וּמְטַלְטְלִין אוֹתָן, בְּגִיזֵּי צֶמֶר וְאֵין מְטַלְטְלִין אוֹתָן
overview.label: The scene:
overview.text: The daf first leaves unresolved whether the mishna's forbidden-when-moist materials refers only to items naturally damp or also to ones wetted from an outside source. A new mishna permits insulating food in clothing, produce, doves' wings, wood shavings, and flax chaff, prompting the Gemara's tangent about Elisha, called 'Man of Wings,' who defiantly wore tefillin under Roman persecution. After settling that Rabbi Yehuda's fine-versus-coarse dispute concerns flax, a further mishna distinguishes movable animal hides from set-aside wool fleece, working out exactly how to retrieve an insulated pot without touching the fleece — and whether this changes for a craftsman's own materials. The daf closes with the classic question of why the primary categories of forbidden Shabbat labor number exactly thirty-nine, tied to the work of building the Tabernacle.

slides.title: 💧 An Unresolved Question About Moisture
slides.label: The dilemma:
slides.text: Do straw, grape pulp, soft rags, and grass become forbidden for insulation only when they are moist on their own, or even when moistened by an outside cause? The Gemara tries to prove the answer from a case of wool plucked 'from between the thighs' of an animal (naturally damp with sweat) — but since that same case fits either reading, the proof from both this mishna and a parallel baraita about garments ultimately fails to settle the question.
slides.hebrewSource: לַחִין מֵחֲמַת עַצְמָן, אוֹ דִילְמָא לַחִין מֵחֲמַת דָּבָר אַחֵר

slides.title: 🕊️ Elisha, Man of Wings
slides.subtitle: A tangent from the mishna's mention of doves' wings as insulation

steps.content: 1️⃣ Rabbi Yannai: donning tefillin requires a clean body, 'like Elisha, Man of Wings' — meaning not to break wind (Abaye) or fall asleep (Rava) while wearing them
2️⃣ Rome decreed death for anyone found wearing tefillin, yet Elisha wore his openly in the marketplace
3️⃣ An official chased him; Elisha pulled the tefillin from his head into his hand and claimed, 'It's a dove's wings'

4️⃣ A miracle occurred — when he opened his hand, they had truly become doves' wings, giving him his name, since Israel is likened to a dove whose only defense is its wings, just as mitzvot alone protect Israel

slides.title: 🌾 Whose Dispute — Wood Shavings or Flax?
slides.subtitle: Rabbi Yehuda distinguishes fine from coarse, but about which material?
rows: Rabbi Yehuda: its legal status is like manure
It actively generates heat, unlike coarse chaff

slides.title: 🧺 Hides May Move; Wool Fleece May Not
slides.subtitle: The new mishna, and how to retrieve a pot without handling set-aside wool

nodes.content: 📜 Mishna: one may insulate food in animal hides (movable) or in wool fleece (not movable)
❓ How does one remove the pot from a basket of fleece without touching the fleece itself?

columns.label: R. Elazar b. Azarya
columns.content: Tip the basket on its side so the fleece falls away — worried the wool might collapse and block replacing the pot

columns.label: The Rabbis
columns.content: Simply lift out the pot; one may replace it afterward too

nodes.content: ⚖️ Craftsman's hides: disputed whether they remain movable like a homeowner's, since a tanner is particular about his own materials — settled by Rabbi Yishmael's father, a tanner, who used to say: 'Bring hides, let's sit on them!'

slides.title: 🔨 Why Thirty-Nine Categories of Labor?
slides.subtitle: Two explanations for the number underlying all of Shabbat's prohibited labors

boxes.title: Corresponds to the Tabernacle
items: Rabbi Chanina bar Chama: the 39 labors match those performed in building the Mishkan
One is liable only for a labor with a true parallel there — sowing, reaping, carrying between domains, and so on

boxes.title: Corresponds to a Word Count
items: Rabbi Shimon b'Rabbi Yosei ben Lakonya: the forms of the word 'melacha' (labor) appear in the Torah exactly 39 times
Rav Yosef's open question: does Joseph's 'to do his labor' count toward that total? Left unresolved (teiku)

callout.label: Worked example:
callout.text: Carrying boards from the wagon to the ground (public to private domain) and back models the prohibition against carrying between domains — exactly as it happened when the Mishkan's boards were transported.

summary.principle: The daf moves from open halakhic questions about insulating materials, through Elisha's tefillin story and the fine points of muktzeh wool and hides, to the foundational teaching that all thirty-nine categories of Shabbat labor trace back to the specific work performed in constructing the Tabernacle.

quiz.q: What question does the Gemara leave unresolved regarding materials like straw and grass that are forbidden for insulation 'when moist'?
o: Whether they may ever be used at all
Whether the prohibition applies only when they are naturally moist, or also when moistened by an outside source
Whether they must be dried before Shabbat
Whether they can insulate cold food
quiz.e: The Gemara raises but cannot conclusively resolve whether 'moist' in the mishna refers only to materials moist by their own nature or also to those wetted by another cause.

quiz.q: Why did Elisha claim to the Roman official that the tefillin in his hand were 'doves' wings'?
o: He was joking with the official
Rome had decreed death for anyone found wearing tefillin, so he removed them and disguised his claim to escape execution — and a miracle made them actually turn into feathers
Tefillin were made of feathers in his time
He had forgotten what tefillin were called
quiz.e: Under Roman persecution wearing tefillin was a capital offense; Elisha's claim was validated by a miracle, giving him the name 'Elisha, Man of Wings.'

quiz.q: According to the resolution reached in the Gemara, which material is the subject of Rabbi Yehuda's fine-versus-coarse dispute?
o: Carpenter's wood shavings
Flax chaff (ne'oret), since a baraita states that fine flax chaff has the legal status of manure
Wool fleece
Animal hides
quiz.e: A baraita proves Rabbi Yehuda's statement concerns flax chaff, teaching that the fine variety generates heat like manure and is therefore forbidden, unlike the coarse variety.

quiz.q: According to the Rabbis (against Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya), how does one remove a pot from a basket insulated with wool fleece?
o: One must tip the basket on its side first
One may simply lift out the pot directly, and may also replace it afterward
The fleece must be removed entirely beforehand
It is forbidden to remove the pot on Shabbat at all
quiz.e: The Rabbis disagree with Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya's more cautious method and hold that one may simply take the pot out and put it back without special precaution.

quiz.q: According to Rabbi Chanina bar Chama, why are there exactly thirty-nine primary categories of forbidden labor on Shabbat?
o: They correspond to the number of days in creation
They correspond to the specific labors that were performed in constructing the Tabernacle (Mishkan)
They correspond to the number of tribes of Israel
There is no reason given
quiz.e: Rabbi Chanina bar Chama teaches that the 39 categories of Shabbat labor all have their source in the actual work performed in building the Tabernacle.
